\chapter{Boolean Analysis — Gate Switching}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.LMN.GateSwitching
\section{Overview}

This module is Step~4 of the LMN argument: it applies Håstad's switching lemma to
individual gates after a Bernoulli$(p)$ restriction. The key bridge results show that,
with high probability, the restriction of a bounded-width $\mathrm{DNF}$ (or $\mathrm{CNF}$)
gate has small decision-tree depth and hence admits a small-width $\mathrm{CNF}$ (or
$\mathrm{DNF}$) representation, and assemble these into union bounds over all gates of a
circuit layer.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{lemma}[Monotonicity of the Bernoulli restriction probability]
\lean{LMN.bernoulliRestrProb_mono}
\label{LMN.bernoulliRestrProb_mono}
\leanok
\uses{SwitchingLemma2.Restriction, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrProb, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrWeight_nonneg'}
\difficulty{4}
Fix a parameter $p \in [0,1]$, and for a predicate $E$ on restrictions of $n$ variables
write $\bbP_p[E]$ for the probability that $E$ holds under a Bernoulli($p$) random
restriction. If $A$ and $B$ are predicates on restrictions such that $A(\rho)$ implies
$B(\rho)$ for every restriction $\rho$, then
\[
  \bbP_p[A] \le \bbP_p[B].
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Bernoulli restriction of a narrow DNF to a narrow CNF, with high probability]
\lean{LMN.switching_bernoulli_gate_to_cnf}
\statementsource{boolean-ch04-dnf-switching-lmn}{
  pdf-fc447f326910-p008-b005,
  pdf-fc447f326910-p012-b004
}
\statementsource{switching-lemma}{
  pdf-b5e074215b9e-p003-b004,
  pdf-b5e074215b9e-p001-b008
}
\label{LMN.switching_bernoulli_gate_to_cnf}
\leanok
\uses{CNF, CNF.eval, CNF.width, DNF, DNF.eval, DNF.width, LMN.bernoulliRestrProb_mono, SwitchingBernoulli.switching_bernoulli_dtDepth_dnf, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrProb, SwitchingLemma2.dtDepth_le_implies_small_dnf_cnf, SwitchingLemma2.restrictFn}
\difficulty{3}
Let $g$ be a DNF formula on $n \ge 1$ variables whose width is at most $w$, where $w \ge
1$, and suppose that within each term of $g$ any two literals having the same variable
are equal and no literal is repeated. Let $l$ be a natural number, and let $p$ be a real
number with $0 < p \le 1$ and $p \le \tfrac{1}{40w}$. Then, under a Bernoulli$(p)$
random restriction $\rho$, the probability that the restricted function $g|_\rho$ is
computed by no CNF formula of width at most $l$ is at most
\[
  \left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right)^{l} + \exp\!\left(-\tfrac{np}{3}\right).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[A Bernoulli-restricted CNF collapses to a narrow DNF]
\lean{LMN.switching_bernoulli_gate_to_dnf_from_cnf}
\statementsource{boolean-ch04-dnf-switching-lmn}{pdf-fc447f326910-p008-b005}
\statementsource{switching-lemma}{
  pdf-b5e074215b9e-p003-b004,
  pdf-b5e074215b9e-p001-b008,
  pdf-b5e074215b9e-p003-b001
}
\label{LMN.switching_bernoulli_gate_to_dnf_from_cnf}
\leanok
\uses{CNF, CNF.eval, CNF.width, DNF, DNF.eval, DNF.width, LMN.bernoulliRestrProb_mono, SwitchingBernoulli.switching_bernoulli_dtDepth_cnf, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrProb, SwitchingLemma2.dtDepth_le_implies_small_dnf_cnf, SwitchingLemma2.restrictFn}
\difficulty{3}
Let $g$ be a CNF formula on $n \ge 1$ variables whose width is at most $w$, where $w \ge
1$, and suppose that within each clause no two distinct literals share a variable and no
literal is repeated. Fix a natural number $l$ and a real parameter $p$ with $0 < p \le
\tfrac{1}{40w}$, so in particular $p \le 1$. Then, drawing a Bernoulli$(p)$ random
restriction $\rho$ on the $n$ variables, the probability that the restricted function
$g|_\rho$ (the function $x \mapsto g(\rho.\mathrm{extend}\,x)$ on the free coordinates)
cannot be computed exactly by any DNF formula of width at most $l$ is at most
\[
  \left(\tfrac12\right)^{l} + \exp\!\left(-\tfrac{np}{3}\right).
\]
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{1}
Let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}$ be a Boolean function, let $\rho$ be a restriction on
the $n$ variables (fixing some coordinates to Boolean values and leaving the rest free),
and write $f\!\restriction_\rho$ for the restricted function $x \mapsto
f(\rho.\mathrm{extend}\,x)$, obtained by evaluating $f$ with the fixed coordinates set
by $\rho$ and the free coordinates supplied by $x$. If $f\!\restriction_\rho$ has
decision-tree depth at most $l$, then there is a CNF formula $\psi$ whose every clause
contains at most $l$ literals and which computes $f\!\restriction_\rho$ on every input,
that is, $\psi(x) = f\!\restriction_\rho(x)$ for all $x \in \{0,1\}^n$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{1}
Let $f : (\bbf_2^{\,n} \to \{0,1\})$ be a Boolean function on $n$ variables and let
$\rho$ be a restriction that fixes some variables to Boolean values and leaves the
others free, so that the restricted function $f|_\rho$ sends a point $x$ to the value of
$f$ on the assignment agreeing with $\rho$ on the fixed coordinates and with $x$ on the
free ones. If $f|_\rho$ has decision-tree depth at most $l$ — that is, some decision
tree of depth at most $l$ computes it — then there exists a DNF formula $\varphi$ whose
width (the maximum number of literals in any of its terms) is at most $l$ and which
agrees with $f|_\rho$ on every input.
\end{theorem}

\uses{DNF, DNF.eval, DNF.width, SwitchingBernoulli.switching_bernoulli_dtDepth_dnf, SwitchingLemma2.Restriction, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrProb, SwitchingLemma2.restrictFn, dtDepth}
\difficulty{6}
Let $D_0,\dots,D_{s-1}$ be $s$ DNF formulas on $n$ Boolean variables, with $n \ge 1$,
each of width at most $w$ where $w \ge 1$, and suppose that in every term of every $D_i$
each variable occurs at most once (no term repeats a literal, and any two literals of a
term on the same variable coincide). Let $p \in \bbr$ satisfy $0 < p \le \tfrac{1}{40w}$
and $p \le 1$. Draw a Bernoulli$(p)$ random restriction $\rho$, which independently
leaves each variable free with probability $p$ and otherwise fixes it to
$\mathtt{false}$ or $\mathtt{true}$ each with probability $(1-p)/2$. Then the
probability that some restricted formula $D_i\!\restriction_\rho$ computes a Boolean
function of decision-tree depth greater than $l$ is at most
\[
  s\left(\left(\tfrac12\right)^{l} + \exp\!\left(-\tfrac{np}{3}\right)\right).
\]
\end{theorem}

\uses{CNF, CNF.eval, CNF.width, DNF, DNF.eval, LMN.restricted_has_small_cnf_of_dtDepth_le, SwitchingLemma2.Restriction, SwitchingLemma2.restrictFn, dtDepth}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ and $l$ be natural numbers, let $\mathrm{gates}_0,\dots,\mathrm{gates}_{s-1}$ be
a family of DNF formulas in $n$ variables, and let $\rho$ be a restriction on the $n$
variables. Suppose that for every index $i$ the restricted function $x \mapsto
(\mathrm{gates}_i)(\rho.\mathrm{extend}\,x)$ has decision-tree depth at most $l$. Then
for every index $i$ there is a CNF formula $\psi$ of width at most $l$ that computes
this restricted function, that is, $\psi(x) =
(\mathrm{gates}_i)(\rho.\mathrm{extend}\,x)$ for every Boolean assignment $x$.
\end{theorem}

\uses{CNF, CNF.eval, CNF.width, DNF, DNF.eval, DNF.width, LMN.bernoulliRestrProb_mono, LMN.restricted_has_small_cnf_of_dtDepth_le, LMN.switching_bernoulli_union_bound, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrProb, SwitchingLemma2.restrictFn}
\difficulty{4}
Let $g_1,\dots,g_{s_2}$ be a family of DNF formulas in $n$ variables, and suppose $n \ge
1$. Fix a width bound $w \ge 1$ and assume each $g_i$ has width at most $w$; assume
moreover that within every term of every $g_i$ the literals are pairwise distinct and
any two literals on the same variable coincide, so that no variable occurs more than
once in a term. Let $p \in \bbr$ satisfy $0 < p \le \frac{1}{40w}$ and $p \le 1$, and
draw a random restriction $\rho$ on the $n$ variables from the Bernoulli($p$)
distribution, in which each variable is independently left free with probability $p$ and
otherwise fixed to $0$ or $1$ each with probability $\frac{1-p}{2}$. Then the
probability that some gate $g_i$ fails to be representable after restriction — that is,
that there is an index $i$ for which the restricted function $g_i\!\restriction_\rho$
(the value $x \mapsto g_i(\rho.\mathrm{extend}\,x)$) is not computed by any CNF formula
of width at most $l$ — is at most
\[
s_2 \cdot \left( \left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right)^{l} + \exp\!\left(-\tfrac{n p}{3}\right)
\right).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Simplified layer-2 CNF replaceability bound]
\lean{LMN.layer2_cnf_replaceability_simplified}
\proofsource{boolean-ch04-dnf-switching-lmn}{pdf-fc447f326910-p012-b004}
\proofsource{switching-lemma}{pdf-b5e074215b9e-p004-b002}
\label{LMN.layer2_cnf_replaceability_simplified}
\leanok
\uses{CNF, CNF.eval, CNF.width, DNF, DNF.eval, DNF.width, LMN.layer2_cnf_replaceability_union_bound, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrProb, SwitchingLemma2.restrictFn}
\difficulty{3}
Fix $n \ge 1$ and let $g_1, \dots, g_{s_2}$ be $s_2 \ge 1$ DNF formulas on $n$ variables
(each a disjunction of terms, each term a conjunction of literals), each of width at
most $w \ge 1$, and such that within every term distinct literals involve distinct
variables (no variable occurs more than once in a term). Let $p$ satisfy $0 < p \le 1$
and $p \le \tfrac{1}{40w}$, and let $\varepsilon > 0$ be such that
$\exp\!\bigl(-\tfrac{np}{3}\bigr) \le \tfrac{\varepsilon}{s_2}$. Then, under a
Bernoulli$(p)$ random restriction $\rho$, the probability that there exists an index $i$
for which the restricted function $g_i|_\rho$ admits no CNF formula of width at most $l$
computing it (equal to it at every input) is at most
\[
  s_2 \cdot \Bigl(\tfrac12\Bigr)^{l} + \varepsilon .
\]
\end{theorem}
